A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MAPLE. Their main text and appendices A–D are readable, and the methods, equations, tables, figures, and case studies can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original Yelp19/Yelp23 experiments, aspect-selection ablations, a PRAG comparison, and generated explanation case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports ERRA comparisons, MAUVE scores, and computational costs.

M1.justification: The architecture, loss forms, aspect sampling and fusion, and retrieval procedure are retained. Two-stage training and zero-shot BART classification already appear in v1 Section 3.6 and Appendix A.1; v2's revised presentation does not establish a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Yelp19 and Yelp23 with the same dataset statistics, aspect inventories, and restaurant explanation tasks. The appendix cases, including French-language personalization, are retained. ERRA and MAUVE extend evaluation within existing coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds ERRA to Table 1 on both datasets. Att2seq, NRT, PETER, and PEPLER remain, while the PRAG comparison and comparator membership in the appendix case studies are unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds MAUVE evaluation in Section 4.2.4 and Tables 1–2. Appendix C.1 changes the reported loss coefficient λ from 2.0 to 1.0; this is a stated setting revision without evidence establishing reruns. The data splits, 10,000-pair evaluation subset, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing aspect-selection ablation with MAUVE, reports preliminary tuning observations that λ=1 trains stably while λ=5 underfits, and adds computational cost analysis. The existing head/tail analysis, t-SNE visualization, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions average MAPLE and review-generation results over five data splits and evaluate PRAG on the first split only. Neither adds confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or seed reporting. MAUVE measures generation quality rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain all pre-existing numerical entries while adding ERRA results and MAUVE scores. MAPLE's new MAUVE scores are 0.0699 on Yelp19 and 0.2183 on Yelp23. Appendix C.2 adds approximately 7/14-hour training times and 0.02-second aspect-recommendation overhead per 200-sample batch. The other quantitative tables and case outputs are unchanged.

T1.justification: The generation loss, aspect predictor, distribution-balanced loss, and feature-metric definitions remain mathematically equivalent. Equations are rearranged or renumbered, with no new theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive formal assumption.

C1.justification: The central claims about diverse, factual, precise explanations, renewed dataset annotations, and MAPLE's usefulness as a discrete retriever remain. V2 foregrounds generation quality and factuality, while relocating the LLM-reader claim from the abstract to the introduction; the contribution scope is substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 replaces v1's explanation that sparse ID updates impede learning with an explanation about preventing overfitting to IDs. V2 also interprets MAUVE as alignment with human text and asserts an advantage for modular extraction/classification in Appendix A.1. The limitations concerning aspect labels and detecting non-factual content remain.

D1.justification: V2 states that code and data are available, replacing v1's release promise, and adds training-time, latency, and tuning information. Conversely, it drops v1's explicit identification of GPT-2 as MAPLE's backbone. Most optimizer, dimensionality, hardware, preprocessing, and retrieval details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds ERRA discussion and explicit comparisons with MAPLE, alongside Sentence-BERT, RAGE, and the citation accompanying MAUVE. It removes the UCEpic discussion/reference and several general model references. These are localized changes within the same research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and parts of the introduction, merges the segmentation and extraction-pipeline subsections, and reorganizes methodology around explicit training stages and inference. Metric subsections are reordered and renamed, the cost appendix is restructured, and language and author information are edited throughout.

P2.justification: V2 adds an introductory illustration and redraws the extraction, training, and retrieval diagrams. Table 1 gains ERRA rows, Tables 1–2 gain MAUVE columns, and multiple tables are resized or restyled. Retained plots and appendix cases are reformatted or relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: ERRA provides a more relevant aspect-aware comparison, while MAUVE complements the earlier diversity and feature metrics. Clearer training presentation, cost reporting, and stated code/data access also help. The gains are limited: Section 5.1 retains an unqualified improvement above 10%, although Table 1's advantage over ERRA is about 4.1% and 2.5%, and the reported λ revision is not reconciled with the retained scores.
